q: Using the scenario above, what is the RPF at the low end (1.5%) of the range?
n: 1.5% × ₱80,000,000 = ₱1,200,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3 (RPF = 1.5% to 3% of PCC); computed)
scenario: A Construction Manager is engaged for a larger mixed-use development with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱80,000,000, compensated under the RPF method of SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3 (1.5% to 3% of the PCC).

q: Under Sec. 9.4 (Manner of Payment), how may the Architect bill and be paid for progress payments during construction?
o: At the Owner's sole discretion, with no formula
Only upon 100% completion
In fixed installments regardless of progress
Proportional to the percentage of progress of completion of the construction work
n: Sec. 9.4 states the Architect may bill and be paid for progress payments during construction proportional to the percentage of progress of completion of the construction work. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.4)

q: Under Sec. 9.2.1, “Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense” is listed as compensation method number...
n: "Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense" is item 9.2.1.2 in the Sec. 9.2.1 list of compensation methods. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.1.2)

q: Using the scenario above, what is the Architect's RPF at the LOW end of the recommended range (1.5% of PCC)?
n: 1.5% × ₱20,000,000 = ₱300,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3 (RPF = 1.5% to 3% of PCC); computed)
scenario: An Architect is engaged as Construction Manager (CM) for a project with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱20,000,000. The Client agrees to compensate the CM using the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) method under SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3, which ranges from 1.5% to 3% of the PCC.

q: Cost Plus Incentive Fee (CPIF) or Cost Plus Adjusted Fee (CPAF), per Sec. 9.2.2.5, is best described as...
o: a fee based solely on a fixed percentage of PCC
a fee paid only upon project completion
a lump-sum contract with no adjustment
a cost-reimbursement type contract with a fee adjusted by “sharing” formulas applied to the difference between final allowable costs and target costs
n: Sec. 9.2.2.5 describes CPIF/CPAF as cost reimbursement type contracts with provisions for a fee that is adjusted by "sharing" formulas applied to the difference between the final allowable costs and the target costs. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.2.5)

q: Per Sec. 9.1.1, the individual CM or the principal of a CM firm must be a State-regulated professional, preferably an Architect who is registered and licensed and who...
o: is directly employed by the PRC Board of Architecture

is a member in good standing of the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA), holds an updated professional identification card, and has managerial capability with extensive construction experience
has passed a separate Construction Management board examination
has at least 10 years' experience solely as a licensed contractor
n: Sec. 9.1.1 requires the Architect to be a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA) with an updated professional identification card, a member in good standing of the IAPOA, with managerial capabilities and extensive experience in construction. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.1.1)

q: A Construction Manager should be motivated to reduce acquisition and operating costs early in a project's life. Which type of provision, per Sec. 9.2.2, should the Owner consider building into the CM's contract at this stage?
o: Cost Plus Fixed Fee only
A flat honorarium with no incentive
Firm Fixed Price only
Incentive-type contract provisions (e.g., Award Fee or Price Adjustment Provisions)
n: Sec. 9.2.2 states incentive-type contracts such as Award Fee Provisions and Price Adjustment Provisions are appropriate during the initial stages of a project, to motivate the CM to reduce acquisition and operating costs. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.2, 9.2.2.1–9.2.2.2)

q: Award Fee Provisions and Price Adjustment Provisions are described in Sec. 9.2.2 as appropriate for which stage of the project?
o: Only during the bidding stage
The later stages of the project
Only after the project is turned over
The initial stages of the project
n: Sec. 9.2.2 states that during the initial stages of the project, incentive-type contracts such as Award Fee Provisions and Price Adjustment Provisions are appropriate. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.2)

q: Using the same scenario, what is the RPF at the high end (3%) of the range?
n: 3% × ₱80,000,000 = ₱2,400,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3 (RPF = 1.5% to 3% of PCC); computed)
scenario: A Construction Manager is engaged for a larger mixed-use development with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱80,000,000, compensated under the RPF method of SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3 (1.5% to 3% of the PCC).

q: If the construction work is not completed, what happens to the pro-rated RPF component per Sec. 9.4?
o: It shall be paid to the Architect by the Client
It is forfeited entirely by the Architect
It is deducted from the Architect's other project fees
It is transferred to the incoming Construction Manager
n: Sec. 9.4 states that should the work not be completed, the pro-rated RPF component shall be paid to the Architect by the Client. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.4)

q: “Mixed Methods of Compensation” appears in Sec. 9.2.1 as item...
n: "Mixed Methods of Compensation" is the sixth and last item listed, 9.2.1.6. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.1.6)

q: Using the same scenario, what is the RPF at the HIGH end of the range (3% of PCC)?
n: 3% × ₱20,000,000 = ₱600,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3 (RPF = 1.5% to 3% of PCC); computed)
scenario: An Architect is engaged as Construction Manager (CM) for a project with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱20,000,000. The Client agrees to compensate the CM using the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) method under SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3, which ranges from 1.5% to 3% of the PCC.

q: Under Cost Plus Fixed Fee (Sec. 9.2.2.6), the Owner pays the Construction Manager...
o: a fee equal to the Full-Time Supervision RPF
a percentage of savings only
a fixed fee plus reimbursement of certain expenses incurred in the performance of basic services
a fixed fee only, with no reimbursement
n: Sec. 9.2.2.6 states the Owner will pay the CM a fixed fee plus reimbursement of certain expenses incurred in the performance of basic services. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.2.6)

q: According to Sec. 9.1.1, which architects are specifically noted as capable of becoming Construction Managers (CMs)?
o: Only Architects who have never worked in construction
Only Architects holding a master's degree in construction management
Architects who are Contractors or who have been in-charge of construction works
Only fresh graduates with no field experience
n: Sec. 9.1.1 states that Architects who are Contractors or who have been in-charge of construction works are capable of becoming Construction Managers. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.1.1)

q: In the later, construction phase of a project, an Owner wants to pay the CM a fee that will remain unaffected even if actual bids differ from the estimate, unless the Owner itself decides to expand the project scope. Which contract type under Sec. 9.2.2 fits this?
o: Cost Plus Incentive Fee
Firm Fixed Price
Award Fee Provisions
Fixed Price Incentive
n: Firm Fixed Price (Sec. 9.2.2.3) fits: the fee is unaffected by variations between estimate and bids or by change orders during construction, unless the Owner initiates an increase in scope. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.2.3)

q: For the later stages of a project, Sec. 9.2.2 states that the appropriate contract types for construction management services are selected according to...
o: the CM's years of experience only
gross estimates and complexity of work
the Architect's personal preference
the number of consultants involved
n: Sec. 9.2.2 states that for the later stages of a project, the preceding types of contracts for construction management services are used according to gross estimates and complexity of work. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.2)

q: Using the scenario above, if the AoR's additional compensation is computed on the percentage basis stated in Sec. 9.5 (5% of the Consultant's fee), how much is the AoR's additional compensation?
scenario: The Client of a project separately hires a structural Consultant whose professional fee is ₱2,000,000. The Architect-of-Record (AoR) coordinates and relates the Consultant's work to the project, per SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.5.

q: Per Sec. 9.5, if the Client hires a Consultant separately, whose account is the Consultant's fee charged to, and who pays it directly?
o: Charged to the Construction Manager's account
Split 50/50 between the Architect and the Client
Charged to the Architect's account, paid by the Architect
Charged to the Client's account, paid directly by the Client
n: Sec. 9.5 states that should the Client hire separately the services of the Consultant, the fee of the Consultant shall be on the account and paid directly by the Client. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.5)

q: What is the purpose of using Construction Management Contracting Concepts (incentive-type contracts) under Sec. 9.2.2?
o: To shift all financial risk to the Architect-of-Record
To increase the Owner's total project cost
To eliminate the need for a Recommended Professional Fee
To motivate the Construction Manager to reduce acquisition and operating costs
n: Sec. 9.2.2 states that to motivate the CM to reduce acquisition and operating costs, CM services can also be compensated using Construction Management Contracting Concepts, a range of incentive-type contracts and provisions. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.2)

q: Using the same scenario, the full recommended range of the Architect's RPF for this project is...
n: At 1.5% and 3% of ₱20,000,000, the RPF ranges from ₱300,000 to ₱600,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3 (RPF = 1.5% to 3% of PCC); computed)
scenario: An Architect is engaged as Construction Manager (CM) for a project with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱20,000,000. The Client agrees to compensate the CM using the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) method under SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3, which ranges from 1.5% to 3% of the PCC.

q: Per Sec. 9.3, the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for Construction Management Services is...
o: 1.5% to 3% of the PCC
5% to 10% of the PCC
10% to 15% of the Cost of Work
1% to 1.5% of the PCC
n: Sec. 9.3 states that CM services can be compensated by a Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) of 1.5% to 3% of the Project Construction Cost (PCC). (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3; cross-ref chunk_06 notes, slide 88)

q: Why are Construction Management services compensated separately from the Architect's regular services?
o: Because CM services may only be performed by engineers
Because the Project Construction Cost already includes the CM fee
Because construction management is not part of the regular services of the Architect
Because the law requires a different professional to render CM services
n: Sec. 9.2 states that since construction management is not part of the regular services of the Architect, the services rendered by the Architect as CM shall be separately compensated. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2)

q: Construction is halted at 70% completion because the Owner decides to discontinue the project. Per Sec. 9.4, who is responsible for paying the Architect the pro-rated RPF for the completed portion of work?
o: The Client
The Contractor
No one; the fee is simply lost
The Construction Manager's insurance carrier
n: Sec. 9.4 states that should the work not be completed, the pro-rated RPF component shall be paid to the Architect by the Client. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.4)

q: Under a Firm Fixed Price arrangement (Sec. 9.2.2.3), the CM's fixed fee is unaffected by variations between the estimate and the bids or by change orders during construction, UNLESS...
o: the project exceeds one year in duration
inflation exceeds 5% annually
the Owner initiates an increase in scope
the CM requests a fee adjustment
n: Sec. 9.2.2.3 states the fee will be unaffected by variations between the estimate and the bids or by change orders during the construction phase unless the Owner initiates an increase in scope. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.2.3)

q: Under the Philippine SPP framework, Sec. 9 — Construction Management Services corresponds to which document?
o: SPP Doc. 204-A
SPP Doc. 206
SPP Doc. 203
SPP Doc. 204-B
n: Sec. 9 covers Construction Management Services, designated SPP Doc. 204-B, distinct from SPP Doc. 204-A (Full-Time Supervision Services). (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9 heading; cross-ref: chunk_06 notes, slide 86)

q: Per Sec. 9.5, the additional compensation for the Architect-of-Record (AoR) for coordinating and relating the Consultant's work can be computed using time-based methods or a percentage basis equivalent to...
o: a flat lump sum fixed by law
5% of the Consultant's fee
10% of the Consultant's fee
1.5% to 3% of the PCC
n: Sec. 9.5 states that additional compensation for the AoR for coordinating and relating the work of the Consultant to the work of the AoR can be computed using time-based methods or percentage basis equivalent to 5% of the Consultant's fee. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.5)

q: Under Award Fee Provisions (Sec. 9.2.2.1), the Construction Manager has the opportunity to obtain an award fee of specified maximum size when...
o: the measured cost-related values meet or exceed the specified target values
the Owner unilaterally decides to reward the CM
the CM works overtime without additional pay
the project finishes on the original completion date regardless of cost
n: Sec. 9.2.2.1 states the CM has the opportunity to obtain an award fee of specified maximum size if the measured cost-related values meet or exceed the specified target values. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.2.1)

q: Continuing the same scenario, suppose the Architect and Client settle on an RPF of ₱600,000 (the high end of the range), and the construction work is currently 40% complete. Per Sec. 9.4, what progress payment is the Architect entitled to bill at this point?
o: ₱600,000 (the full fee)
₱0, since the project is not yet complete
n: Sec. 9.4 allows billing proportional to percentage of progress of completion: 40% × ₱600,000 = ₱240,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.4; computed)
scenario: An Architect is engaged as Construction Manager (CM) for a project with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱20,000,000. The Client agrees to compensate the CM using the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) method under SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3, which ranges from 1.5% to 3% of the PCC.

q: How does the Recommended Professional Fee for Construction Management Services (SPP 204-B) compare to that of Full-Time Supervision Services (SPP 204-A)?
o: Construction Management has no RPF; only Full-Time Supervision does
They are identical, both at 1% to 1.5% of PCC
Full-Time Supervision's RPF is higher because it requires daily site presence
Construction Management's RPF (1.5% to 3% of PCC) is higher than Full-Time Supervision's (1% to 1.5% of PCC)
n: Construction Management Services (SPP 204-B) carries an RPF of 1.5% to 3% of PCC, which is a higher range than Full-Time Supervision Services (SPP 204-A) at 1% to 1.5% of PCC — reflecting the broader managerial/consulting scope of CM versus the narrower daily site-presence role of full-time supervision. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.3, cross-referenced with SPP Doc. 204-A; chunk_06 notes, slides 85 & 88)

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the methods of compensation for Construction Management Services listed under Sec. 9.2.1?
o: Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses
Retainer
Percentage of Construction Cost Project
Lump Sum or Fixed Fee
n: Sec. 9.2.1 lists six methods (Percentage of Construction Cost Project, Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense, Professional Fee Plus Expenses, Lump Sum or Fixed Fee, Per Diem/Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses, and Mixed Methods). "Retainer" is not among them — it appears instead in the Specialized Architectural Services (SPP Doc. 203) list. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.1; cross-ref SPP Doc. 203 methods list)

q: The Client separately engages a structural Consultant. The Architect-of-Record spends significant time coordinating and integrating the Consultant's output into the project. Per Sec. 9.5, may the AoR seek additional compensation for this coordination, and how may it be computed?
o: No, coordination is unpaid and treated as part of basic services
Yes, but only as a flat government-mandated fee
No, only the Client's Consultant may bill for this
Yes, computed using time-based methods or a percentage equivalent to 5% of the Consultant's fee
n: Sec. 9.5 allows additional compensation for the AoR for coordinating and relating the Consultant's work, computed using time-based methods or a percentage basis equivalent to 5% of the Consultant's fee. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.5)

q: Under Fixed Price Incentive (Sec. 9.2.2.4), the CM's fixed fee is adjusted according to...
o: the difference between the final allowable costs and the target costs
the Architect's professional fee schedule
the prevailing interest rate
the number of change orders issued
n: Sec. 9.2.2.4 states the Owner pays the CM a fixed fee which is adjusted according to the difference between the final allowable costs and the target costs. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.2.4)

q: Who may serve as the Construction Manager (CM) on a project, per SPP Doc. 204-B?
o: Only a corporation registered with the SEC
Only the Architect-of-Record personally
Only a licensed Civil Engineer
An individual or a firm
n: Sec. 9.1 states that the Construction Manager may be an individual or a firm. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.1)

q: An Architect is offered the role of Construction Manager on a project. He is a Registered and Licensed Architect but has never had managerial responsibility for construction works. Per Sec. 9.1.1, is he suited for the role as described?
o: Yes, but only if he is under 40 years old
No — Sec. 9.1.1 also expects managerial capability and extensive experience in construction, in addition to being a State-regulated professional in good standing
No, only civil engineers may serve as Construction Managers
Yes, RLA status alone is sufficient regardless of managerial or construction experience
n: Sec. 9.1.1 requires the Architect-CM to be an RLA in good standing of the IAPOA and to have managerial capabilities with extensive experience in the field of construction — RLA status alone does not satisfy the qualification. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.1.1)

q: Under Price Adjustment Provisions (Sec. 9.2.2.2), the contract price is adjusted...
o: at the sole discretion of the Consultant
only downward, never upward
upward or downward in accordance with a prearranged formula
only by court order
n: Sec. 9.2.2.2 states the contract price is adjusted upward or downward in accordance with a prearranged formula; the operating and support cost factor provision gives a direct incentive on operating and support costs. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-B, Sec. 9.2.2.2)
